Symphony (OpenAI) vs AMOA (AI Maestro Orchestrator Agent) — In-Depth Comparison

Generated: 2026-05-06 00:38 +0200 Symphony source: https://github.com/openai/symphony (commit fetched 2026-05-06) AMOA source: /Users/emanuelesabetta/Code/EMASOFT-ORCHESTRATOR-AGENT/ai-maestro-orchestrator-agent/ v1.6.12 Scope: Symphony's SPEC.md + 5 sub-skills (commit, pull, push, land, debug) + Elixir WORKFLOW.md reference implementation. Linear-specific skill ignored per user instruction. AMOA's main agent + 21 skills + 6 agents + 15 commands + 4 hooks + 5 docs.

---

0. TL;DR for the impatient reader

Decision for finding-1

Symphony and AMOA are both "orchestrate coding agents" systems, but they answer different questions:

QuestionSymphony's answerAMOA's answer
What runs the loop?A long-lived OS daemon polling the tracker every N msA Claude Code main-agent turn; loop ticks come from a Stop-hook + /orchestrator-loop skill
Where does the agent run?Subprocess spawned by the daemon, isolated under workspace.root/<id>/A separate Claude Code session reachable via AI Maestro AMP messaging
What is the source of truth?Repo-owned WORKFLOW.md (front-matter config + prompt template) re-loaded on file changeHard-coded skills + design/state/exec-phase.md + GitHub Issue labels + AI Maestro registry
What is the per-issue contract?One persistent ticket comment ("Codex Workpad") with structured sectionsThe GitHub Issue body + per-task task-requirements-document stored elsewhere
What does the agent execute?A Codex turn that may continue up to max_turns=20 on the same threadA subagent / remote agent that returns a final report
How many roles are there?1 (Codex agent in a workspace) plus 1 daemon (Symphony)5 governance roles (AMAMA, AMCOS, AMOA, AMIA, AMAA) plus N implementer/tester agents

One-line takeaway: Symphony is a runtime contract (a small surface, formally specified, with deterministic dispatch / retry / reconcile state machines). AMOA is a role-and-process system (a much larger surface, expressed as instructions, with rich governance and human-in-loop stages).

The most valuable transfer ideas are: (a) the WORKFLOW.md repo-owned contract, (b) the persistent "Workpad" comment with strict template, (c) the explicit run-attempt state machine + retry/backoff formula, (d) max_turns continuation semantics, (e) the JSON snapshot HTTP API, and (f) the pull/push/commit/land/debug workflow skill set. The least valuable ideas are: the 1-tracker-only assumption, the implicit reliance on git add -A in the commit skill, and the hand-rolled stall watcher script (land_watch.py) that AMOA can replace with its hook system.

1. Architectural Comparison

Decision for finding-2

1.1 What each system actually IS

DimensionSymphonyAMOA
Software typeStandalone OS daemon (Elixir reference impl) — "scheduler/runner and tracker reader"Claude Code plugin (Markdown skill files + Python hook scripts)

Reference implementationElixir/OTP service in elixir/ subtree, validated by mix test + dialyzerClaude Code itself executes the skills; validation via validate_plugin.py (CPV)
Trigger modelCron-style (polling.interval_ms, default 30 s) + filesystem watch on WORKFLOW.mdHuman prompt → Claude turn; recurring "ticks" come from /orchestrator-loop and the Stop hook re-firing the turn
Concurrency modelBounded global concurrency (max_concurrent_agents=10) + per-state caps; one OS subprocess per issueBounded by AI Maestro registered agent count; each agent is a separate Claude session
State storageIn-memory only (no DB); recovery is tracker+filesystem drivendesign/state/exec-phase.md (YAML) + GitHub Project + AI Maestro inbox
LifetimeLong-running daemon, restart only for upgradePer-Claude-Code session; durable cron heartbeat keeps it alive
Human in the loopOptional — Human Review is a workflow state, not a built-in dependencyMandatory at multiple points: AMAMA approves design, user approves big-task PRs

1.2 Layered architecture map

Symphony's layers (from SPEC §3.2):

┌─ Policy Layer ─────────────────────  WORKFLOW.md prompt body
├─ Configuration Layer ──────────────  YAML front-matter → typed getters
├─ Coordination Layer ───────────────  Orchestrator: poll/dispatch/retry/reconcile
├─ Execution Layer ──────────────────  workspace + Codex subprocess
├─ Integration Layer ────────────────  Linear adapter
└─ Observability Layer ──────────────  structured logs + optional HTTP/dashboard

AMOA's effective layers (reverse-engineered from skills + docs):

┌─ Policy Layer ─────────────────────  ROLE_BOUNDARIES.md + RULE 14 + governance graph (R6)
├─ Process Layer ────────────────────  FULL_PROJECT_WORKFLOW.md (6 phases, 24 steps)
├─ Coordination Layer ───────────────  AMOA main agent + 21 skills (orchestration patterns)
├─ Execution Layer ──────────────────  Subagents (in-process) + remote agents (via AMP)
├─ Integration Layer ────────────────  GitHub CLI + GitHub Projects V2 GraphQL
└─ Observability Layer ──────────────  GitHub Issues, kanban, AI Maestro inbox, hook stdout

Key contrast: Symphony has a clean "Coordination Layer" with formal state transitions; AMOA's coordination layer is a bag of skills the model is asked to compose, with state externalised into GitHub Issues and hook-checked YAML files. Symphony's design is enforceable at compile time / by tests; AMOA's design is enforceable mostly at runtime (hooks, validators) and by trusting the model's adherence to rules.

2. Workflow Comparison — Step by Step

Decision for finding-3

This section walks through identical work — "implement an issue" — through both systems.

2.1 Symphony per-issue workflow (from SPEC §16 + WORKFLOW.md)

1.  Tick fires (every polling.interval_ms = 5000 ms in WORKFLOW.md, default 30000)
2.  Reconcile running issues
    - Stall detection: kill if no event for stall_timeout_ms (300 000 ms)
    - Refresh tracker state for all running IDs
    - If terminal → terminate worker + clean workspace
    - If non-active → terminate worker (no cleanup)
3.  Validate dispatch config (workflow file present, tracker key set, etc.)
4.  Fetch candidate issues in active states
5.  Sort by priority asc, created_at oldest first, identifier
6.  For each candidate while slots > 0:
    - Skip if already running/claimed
    - Skip if Todo with non-terminal blockers
    - Spawn worker:
       a. workspace_manager.create_for_issue() → may run after_create hook
       b. run before_run hook
       c. Launch codex app-server via `bash -lc <codex.command>`, cwd = workspace
       d. Initialise Codex thread (thread_id), start turn 1 with rendered prompt
       e. Loop up to max_turns:
          - Send prompt (turn 1: full template; later: continuation-only)
          - Stream events to orchestrator (token usage, rate limits, turn outcome)
          - On turn success → re-fetch issue state
          - If still active and turn < max_turns → next turn on SAME thread
          - Else break
       f. Stop session, run after_run hook (best-effort)
       g. Worker exits "normal"
    - Orchestrator schedules a 1-second continuation retry
7.  On worker abnormal exit:
    - Backoff: delay = min(10000 * 2^(attempt-1), max_retry_backoff_ms = 300 000)
    - Retry via timer
8.  Operator changes WORKFLOW.md → live reload, applies to next dispatch

The Codex agent inside the workspace then follows the prompt body (WORKFLOW.md line 39+):

Step 0:  Determine ticket state, route to matching flow
Step 1:  Find/create persistent "## Codex Workpad" comment
         - Reconcile (check off, expand plan)
         - Add environment stamp: <host>:<abs-workdir>@<short-sha>
         - Add Plan/Acceptance/Validation/Notes/Confusions sections
Step 2:  Execute (Todo → In Progress → Human Review)
         - Reproduce first
         - Run `pull` skill → record sync result + HEAD short SHA
         - Implement, validate, run PR feedback sweep (BLOCKING all reviewer comments)
         - When green → move to Human Review
Step 3:  Human Review → poll → on approval, follow `land` skill (loop until merged)
Step 4:  Rework → close PR, drop workpad, fresh branch, full restart (NOT incremental)

2.2 AMOA per-issue workflow (from FULL_PROJECT_WORKFLOW.md)

Phase 1 — Project Creation:
  1. AMAMA creates project, sends requirements to AMCOS
  2. AMCOS evaluates, suggests team, AMAMA approves
  3. AMCOS creates/configures agents, assigns to team
  4. AMCOS notifies AMAMA "team ready"

Phase 2 — Design:
  6. AMAMA sends requirements to AMAA (Architect)
  7. AMAA writes design document (architecture, modules, specs)
  8. AMAA submits design to AMAMA
  9. AMAMA + USER approve design (rejection loops back to AMAA)

Phase 3 — Task Planning:
  10. AMOA decomposes design into actionable tasks
  11. AMOA writes task-requirements-document per task
  12. AMOA orders tasks, identifies parallelism
  13. AMOA creates GitHub issues, populates kanban, assigns agents
  14. AMOA notifies each agent (mandatory ACK)
  15. Implementer feedback loop → design-change-request to AMAA

Phase 4 — Implementation:
  17. Implementer agents start work; report "in development"
  18. AMOA moves task Todo → In Progress
  19. Agent completes → AMOA interview → approval to PR

Phase 5 — Integration:
  20. AMOA → AMIA: PR review request
  21. AMIA reviews, runs tests, merges or rejects
  22. Failed PR: feedback to agent, return to In Progress

Phase 6 — Completion:
  23. AMOA moves task: ai-review → (human-review for big tasks) → merge-release → done
  24. AMOA reports to AMAMA, assigns next task

The orchestrator-loop heartbeat (from amoa-orchestration-loop) is itself enforced by:

  • /orchestrator-loop --max-iterations N — the model self-loops
  • Stop hook blocks Claude Code exit until ALL_TASKS_COMPLETE signal
  • UserPromptSubmit hook (amoa-polling-reminder) reminds when polling is overdue
  • PreToolUse hook (amoa-instruction-verification-check) blocks agent reports if verification incomplete

The bigger meta-gap: AMOA has no skill set for the implementer. Its 21 skills are all for the orchestrator. The commit/pull/push/land/debug quintet from Symphony is exactly what the implementer agents need.

5. Adoption Recommendations (Ordered by Priority)

Decision for finding-6

5.1 Tier 1 — Adopt immediately (low cost, high value)

  1. Add Workpad pattern to AMOA
  • What: A persistent ## AMOA Workpad GitHub issue comment per task with sections: env-stamp / Plan / Acceptance / Validation / Notes / Confusions.
  • Why: AMOA currently writes a task-requirements-document and then separately updates GitHub Issue body and labels. Reviewers have no single place to see live progress. The Workpad becomes the contract.
  • Where: Update amoa-orchestration-patterns and amoa-implementer-interview-protocol.
  • Cost: ~half a day to write the template + update 2 skills.
  1. Add commit/pull/push/land/debug skill quintet for implementers
  • What: Five new skills as adapted from Symphony, with git add -A stripped, GitHub-only paths, and AMOA's role boundaries respected.
  • Why: Closes the "no implementer skills" gap. Without these, every implementer agent reinvents commit / push / land workflow.
  • Where: New plugin or new skills under amoa-. Owner of land is debatable — likely AMIA's responsibility, but the pattern is universal.
  • Cost: 1–2 days to adapt and validate.
  1. Add [amoa] (or [amia]) prefix to every agent-generated PR comment
  • What: Trivial naming convention. Update amoa-developer-communication and amoa-implementer-interview-protocol.
  • Why: Lets reviewers grep [amoa] to find every agent comment; fixes the "is this human or AI" ambiguity.
  • Cost: Half-hour rule update.
  1. Add inline-reply correctness rule for PR review comments
  • What: Document that PR review comment replies MUST use gh api repos/{owner}/{repo}/pulls/<pr>/comments -F in_reply_to=<numeric-comment-id>, NOT gh pr comment (which posts to the issue thread).
  • Why: Real bug — in_reply_to requires the PR number in the URL and the numeric review-comment id (not the GraphQL PRRC_… node id). This is exactly the kind of one-shot detail a model gets wrong without explicit instruction.
  • Where: amoa-developer-communication/references/.
  • Cost: 30 minutes.
  1. Add "every actionable PR comment is blocking until reply or pushback" rule
  • What: Replace AMOA's "4 loops" with Symphony's per-comment tracking model.
  • Why: "4 loops" can pass while leaving comments unanswered. Per-comment tracking guarantees no comment is silently dropped.
  • Where: amoa-implementer-interview-protocol, amoa-verification-patterns.
  • Cost: Half-day to update + validate against existing examples.
  1. Add "out-of-scope improvements become a separate Backlog issue" rule
  • What: Lift verbatim from Symphony WORKFLOW.md L86–91.
  • Why: AMOA mentions scope discipline but doesn't enforce the "create Backlog issue" outlet, so agents either expand scope or silently drop ideas.
  • Where: amoa-orchestration-guardrails.
  • Cost: 30 minutes.
  1. Adopt the exponential backoff formula
  • What: Replace AMOA's "reassign once, then escalate" with delay = min(10000 * 2^(attempt-1), 300_000) ms. Schedule a 1-second continuation retry after every normal completion.
  • Why: Standard formula, well-tested. Gives /orchestration-status predictable retry timing.
  • Where: amoa-progress-monitoring, amoa-orchestration-loop.
  • Cost: Half-day of changes + tests.

5.2 Tier 2 — Adopt with light design (medium cost, high value)

  1. Run-attempt state machine
  • What: Track each task through explicit phases: PreparingContext → Assigned → Acknowledged → Implementing → PRDraft → PRReview → Merged (or Failed / Stalled / CanceledByReassignment). Mirror Symphony's §7.2.
  • Why: AMOA today uses GitHub labels for state, which mixes "what column on the kanban" with "what life-cycle phase the work is in." Separating them lets /orchestration-status say why something is in In Progress (e.g. waiting for ACK vs writing code vs waiting for CI).
  • Where: New section in amoa-progress-monitoring/references/.
  • Cost: 1 day design + 1 day to wire into hook scripts and /orchestration-status.
  1. Stall detection with explicit stall_timeout_ms
  • What: Add an opt-in setting on each task: "if no progress event for N minutes, escalate." Default 15 min for normal tasks, 60 min for big tasks. Replace the implicit "10–15 min" polling with formal thresholds.
  • Where: amoa-progress-monitoring + new stall_timeout_ms field in task-requirements-document front-matter.
  • Cost: 1 day.
  1. Token + runtime accounting
  • What: Aggregate Anthropic token usage per task (from /cost snapshots or hook reads) into design/state/exec-phase.md. Surface in /orchestration-status.
  • Why: AMOA currently has zero visibility into cost. With tiered models (Haiku/Sonnet/Opus) being recommended in CLAUDE.md, you need accounting to validate whether the recommendations are followed.
  • Where: New skill amoa-cost-accounting; add Python helper to read Claude Code's daily usage JSON.
  • Cost: 2 days + dependency on Claude Code's usage telemetry (which the user already has — see tldr-stats skill in available skills list).
  1. Conflict-resolution skill (port pull skill's best practices)
  • What: Document zdiff3 setup, git diff :1: :2: :3: for base-vs-ours-vs-theirs, the "decide intent first, then edit" heuristic, and the "when to ask the user (keep to a minimum)" list.
  • Where: New amoa-conflict-resolution skill or reference under amoa-developer-communication.
  • Cost: Half-day (mostly text adaptation).

5.3 Tier 3 — Adopt only if scope expands (high cost or scope-dependent)

  1. AMOA-WORKFLOW.md repo-owned contract
  • What: A single per-project file that mirrors Symphony's WORKFLOW.md for the AMOA model: front-matter with team registry path, kanban project ID, polling cadence, max-concurrent-agents, etc.; body with the project-specific orchestration prompt overrides.
  • Why: Lets each project version-control its orchestration policy (right now, every project re-invokes the global plugin and gets the same behavior).
  • Caution: Symphony's choice to bundle runtime config + prompt in ONE file is questionable — split into amoa-config.yaml + optional amoa-prompt-overrides.md.
  • Cost: 3–5 days (config schema + parser + docs).
  1. HTTP JSON API for status snapshot
  • What: Optional amoa-server skill / standalone Python HTTP server exposing /api/v1/state and /api/v1/<issue> over loopback.
  • Why: Useful only if external tools (dashboards, IDE extensions, monitoring) need machine-readable status.
  • Caution: Significant infra. Don't build until you have a consumer.
  1. Live filesystem watch + dynamic reload of skills
  • What: Symphony's auto-reload on WORKFLOW.md change. AMOA already has /reload-plugins for plugin-scoped hooks; adding watch could trigger that automatically.
  • Caution: The user already has a documented constraint: project .claude/settings.json hook edits require a full session restart (see CLAUDE.md). Adding auto-reload would either need to respect this constraint or actively cancel itself. Not worth the complexity unless the workflow file lives outside settings.json.
  1. Conformance test matrix
  • What: Translate Symphony's §17 into an amoa-conformance.yaml test plan, run by CPV.
  • Why: AMOA's CPV does structural validation (skills have descriptions, etc.) but no behavioural conformance check.
  • Cost: 1–2 weeks (it's a small test framework).

5.4 Tier 4 — Reject (Symphony's choice is wrong for AMOA)

  1. Single-tracker assumption — AMOA already does GitHub well; don't regress.
  2. Workspace cleanup on Rework — Symphony's "drop branch + workpad" approach loses history; AMOA's reassign + handoff doc is better.
  3. In-memory state only — AMOA's YAML state file recovers cleanly; keep it.
  4. git add -A — Hard rule violation; never adopt.
  5. Bundling code-writes into the orchestrator agent — Violates AMOA's RULE 15 (orchestrator does not implement). Symphony has no equivalent role separation, so it conflates the two; AMOA must NOT collapse them.

---

6. Risk Analysis of the Most Important Adoption Targets

Decision for finding-7

6.1 Workpad pattern (recommended Tier 1)

Pro: Single source of truth for live state; reviewers stop hunting through scattered docs; the structure (Plan/Acceptance/Validation/Notes/Confusions) is battle-tested in Symphony's actual deployments at OpenAI.

Con: A persistent comment on a GitHub issue is mutable and can be edited away. Symphony mitigates this by treating the workpad as authoritative inside the running agent's loop. AMOA needs the same discipline + a hook that checks "did the workpad just disappear?"

Mitigation: Add a PostToolUse hook (or extend amoa-file-tracker) to detect deletion / drastic shrinkage of the Workpad comment and re-create from history.

6.2 Per-comment "blocking until reply" PR sweep (recommended Tier 1)

Pro: Closes a real loophole — AMOA's "4 loops" can pass while a critical comment is unanswered.

Con: Some PR comments are not actionable (e.g., a thumbs-up). Symphony solves this by making the agent classify each comment as correctness / design / style / clarification / scope (land/SKILL.md L215). Adopting just the "blocking" rule without the classification rule will produce false negatives.

Mitigation: Adopt both — the blocking rule AND the classification rule, in the same change.

6.3 Run-attempt state machine (recommended Tier 2)

Pro: Diagnostic gold. /orchestration-status becomes much more informative.

Con: AMOA already has the 8-column kanban + state labels + phase in YAML. Adding a fourth state dimension risks confusion.

Mitigation: Make the state-machine a sub-state of the kanban column. E.g. In Progress → (Assigned → Acknowledged → Implementing → PRDraft). Document the mapping explicitly.

6.4 commit/pull/push/land/debug skills (recommended Tier 1)

Pro: Closes the "AMOA has no implementer-side skills" gap. The skills are short (each <200 lines) and can be added without disrupting the orchestrator.

Con: They will live as instructions for implementer agents (who today are external, AMP-coordinated). If implementers don't load AMOA's plugin, they won't see the skills. Two solutions:

  • (a) Make the skills part of a shared plugin loaded by all team agents.
  • (b) Bundle the skill text inside the task-requirements-document AMOA generates per task.

Mitigation: Solution (a) is cleaner; solution (b) is a fallback if shared-plugin distribution isn't ready.

7. Concrete First-Sprint Plan (if you want to start adopting)

Decision for finding-8

A two-week sprint that maximises ROI:

Week 1

  1. (Day 1) Write the Workpad template — one Markdown file with the canonical sections — and a one-page rule "AMOA Workpad Template" added to amoa-orchestration-patterns. Update amoa-implementer-interview-protocol to require interviewees to write into the Workpad.
  2. (Day 2–3) Write the five implementer skills (amoa-commit-hygiene, amoa-pull-sync, amoa-push-publish, amoa-pr-landing, amoa-debug-runs), strip every git add -A, replace with explicit-file staging, point all GitHub APIs at the right endpoints (pulls/<n>/comments not issues/<n>/comments for inline replies).
  3. (Day 4) Add the four small rules: [amoa] prefix on PR comments, "every actionable PR comment blocks until reply", "out-of-scope = new Backlog issue", classification of each PR comment into 5 categories.
  4. (Day 5) Replace ad-hoc retry policy with min(10000 * 2^(n-1), 300_000) formula; add the 1-second continuation retry after every successful agent return.

Week 2

  1. (Day 1–2) Design the run-attempt state machine; map states to existing kanban columns; add to amoa-progress-monitoring.
  2. (Day 3) Add stall_timeout_ms field to task-requirements-document; wire amoa_check_remote_agents.py to escalate on threshold breach.
  3. (Day 4) Add token-usage accounting reader (consume Claude Code's stats API or tldr-stats), aggregate to /orchestration-status.
  4. (Day 5) Update CPV validators to require Workpad presence; add conformance tests for the new skills.

After the sprint:

  • AMOA has a single canonical task contract (Workpad).
  • Implementers have a uniform git workflow.
  • Retry / stall semantics are formalised.
  • Cost visibility appears for the first time.
  • PR review process has explicit blocking semantics.

8. Final Verdict

Decision for finding-9
AspectSymphonyAMOAWinner
Specification rigourFormal RFC 2119Behavioural proseSymphony
Per-issue isolationWorkspace + sandbox + hooksNoneSymphony
Scope of role separationOne role (Codex agent)Five roles + governance graphAMOA
Human-in-loop integrationOptional handoff stateMandatory at multiple gatesAMOA (for serious work)
Inter-agent messagingStdio app-serverAMP messaging across sessionsAMOA
Tracker integrationPluggable but only LinearNative GitHubAMOA for GitHub shops
Implementer-side skills5 strong skills (commit/pull/push/land/debug)NoneSymphony
Orchestrator-side skillsNone (it's a daemon)21 detailed skillsAMOA
Cost visibilityToken accounting in specNoneSymphony
Verification rigourPer-comment blocking + classification"4 loops" (looser)Symphony
Replacement / handoffNoneExplicit protocol + handoff docAMOA
Live config reloadYes (filesystem watch)ManualSymphony
Operational dashboardOptional HTTP API + JSON snapshotMarkdown CLISymphony for tooling, AMOA for human use
Plugin packaging / distributionNoneFull Claude Code plugin pipelineAMOA
Stop-gate enforcementNoneStop hook + ALL_TASKS_COMPLETEAMOA

Synthesis: Symphony is a narrower, cleaner runtime contract whose strongest contributions to AMOA are the Workpad pattern, the implementer-side skill set (commit/pull/push/land/debug), the run-attempt state machine, the exponential backoff formula, the token accounting model, and the per-comment blocking PR review rule. AMOA's strongest assets — multi-role governance, AMP messaging, agent replacement, GitHub-native integration, plugin packaging — should be preserved and not sacrificed in any port.

The ideal end-state is "AMOA + Symphony's discipline at the per-task contract layer + Symphony's implementer skills + Symphony's accounting / retry maths" — keeping AMOA's process and governance machinery intact while bolting on the runtime rigor Symphony has spent SPEC.md formalising.

Appendix B — Glossary

Decision for finding-11
  • AMP — AI Maestro Protocol; messaging layer between Claude Code sessions
  • AMOA — AI Maestro Orchestrator Agent (one of five role-specialised plugins)
  • AMAMA / AMCOS / AMOA / AMIA / AMAA — Manager / Chief-of-Staff / Orchestrator / Integrator / Architect roles
  • CPV — Claude Plugins Validation (the validator suite shipped in this workspace)
  • Workpad — Symphony's name for the persistent ticket comment that holds Plan / Acceptance / Validation / Notes / Confusions
  • max_turns — Symphony's per-worker cap on consecutive Codex turns sharing one thread (default 20)
  • stall_timeout_ms — Symphony's "no event for N ms = kill" threshold (default 300 000)
  • R6 — AMOA's communication-graph version (governs which roles can message which)
  • RULE 14 — AMOA's "user requirements are immutable" iron rule
  • RULE 15 — AMOA's "orchestrator must NOT implement" iron rule
  • kanban "8-column" — AMOA's columns: Backlog / Todo / In Progress / AI Review / Human Review / Merge/Release / Done / Blocked
